title: Writing an investigation instruction
body:
You are authoring this N (investigation-instruction) directly instead of
the server emitting a fixed template. Reflect the actual context of this group and
the requirement it serves. A good N does NOT investigate or implement anything — it
DIRECTS the investigation the paired NR will carry out. Cover:
- Purpose/background: why this investigation is needed (tie it to the driving R/B).
- Investigation scope: the concrete questions the NR must answer + the code/areas to inspect.
- Expected output: what the NR should conclude (root cause, coordinates, reuse anchors).
Keep it an instruction: name what to find out, not the findings themselves — those
belong in the NR that follows. Do NOT modify source code in this step.

When the mention has an 'Instruction to include next document header' section, include the
next-document header exactly as given there (next_type / project / module / group / title / target_id).
When the mention asks you to write into an existing document (edit), it has no such section: keep
that document's existing header (front matter) as it is and add no next-document header.
On submit this instruction is auto-approved (non-{M,CH}) like any managed instruction and
the unmanned chain proceeds to its paired report step.
